result.title: Nunchi: Ears Help Eyes in Multi-Party Conversations
result.summary: Identifying whom a person looks at is central to understanding multi-party conversations, yet gaze geometry alone becomes ambiguous as more people appear. Conversations offer cues that geometry lacks, such as who is speaking and what is said, but no gaze dataset provides them for many multi-party scenes. We introduce SORBET, a benchmark of 3,340 samples from 1,578 clips with synchronized speech, transcripts, and attended person labels, covering more multi-party scenes than existing gaze datasets. Prior gaze models struggle to use these cues, which come in different forms, must be linked to the right person, and can conflict with gaze geometry. We propose Nunchi, a framework that constructs a text prompt from the transcript and the outputs of gaze and speaker models, links every cue to the candidates with shared labels, and lets a vision-language model (VLM) weigh gaze geometry against conversational cues to identify the attended person. Nunchi outperforms the strongest existing method by 4.8 percentage points. On SORBET, conversational cues help whereas additional visual cues do not, and the gains hold across three VLMs, with automatic transcripts, and on two existing datasets.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SORBET 基准（1,578 个片段共 3,340 个样本，含同步语音、转写与被注视者标签）及 Nunchi 框架：把转写与 gaze、说话人模型输出构造成文本提示并关联到候选人，由 VLM 权衡几何线索与对话线索来判定被注视者。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把视觉几何线索序列化为文本、并与语言线索冲突仲裁的做法，可供核查 VLM 是否转而依赖文本旁路、弱化视觉证据使用，与 LVR 的视觉证据筛选和信息坍缩问题相关，但属多 party 注视推断任务，联系需较多核查。
